admission.justification: The interval design was weighed and rejected on burst grounds, and the choice binds every future workspace writer.

alternatives.option: Admit every append under the river lock, cutting oldest whole rows to 8 MiB first.
alternatives.reason: A size read under the already-held lock costs nothing an interval would save, and the bound holds after every append.

alternatives.option: Check size on a sixty-second interval.
alternatives.reason: Bursts pass between checks while the file stands over the ceiling.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Lock contention ever dominates append latency and a cheaper exact check exists.

consequences: Every workspace writer takes the river lock per append; oversized rows are refused and counted rather than written.
context: Architect F01 ruling: a once-a-minute size check lets any burst pass the 16 MiB ceiling, and the age compactor cannot remove young rows.
decider: Architect, F01 ruling on MIK-R114@v1, adopted by the leaf.
